dedupe_keys.name: jemss jl julia emergency medical services simulation

description: JEMSS.jl is a Julia package for simulating emergency medical services (EMS): calls arrive at locations and times, ambulances are dispatched from stations, drive over a road network to the call, may transport patients to hospital and return, and the simulation reports response times and ambulance utilisation. It supports studies of dispatch rules, ambulance relocation (move-up) policies and station locations. It is published by the uoa-ems-research group, whose name and Auckland example point to the University of Auckland. It ships city-like models of Auckland (New Zealand), Edmonton (Canada), Manhattan (United States) and Utrecht (Netherlands); the README says these are not exact replicas of the cities, and a linked document gives their sources. Any other area can be modelled by supplying ambulances, calls, stations, hospitals and a road network through a configuration file; resolution is the individual call and road link. It is a Julia package installed from GitHub (tags up to v1.3.6), with example scripts and a browser animation that needs the user's own Mapbox access token. Licence: Apache 2.0, free. Caveats: the bundled city data are approximations, the first run precomputes all-pairs shortest paths, and there is no graphical model builder. Simulation uses: emergency response planning, optimisation of ambulance deployment and capacity planning of EMS fleets. Related: the NHS ambulance handover simulation (catalogued as model-ambulance-des-nhsx) models the hospital end of the same process.
